rationale: Where the frontier is: the courtyard. The diorama is called The Courtyard, the walled garden is the centre-left third of every wide shot, and #94 measured what shots/wide.png shows — the lawn's own kinds inside the wall hold a MEDIAN 0.25 person at 10 h, 1.0 at 13 h, 2.0 at 16 h on a summer day (seed 42 days 6–7: nobody), while the plaza (#92), the cafe (#74), the concert green and the warm evening (#79) all fill because each got its own source with places as its cap. The courtyard is the last population still on the iteration-1 model: ONE spawnAgent(room) roll under `capacity`, whose default branch is a ring walker who transits and leaves, with the staying kinds as 10–12% shares of that roll. That is the weakest system in the town by the run's own numbers, and costSpike says rung 2 is spent — so this batch is RUNG 6: retire and rebuild it (b95, the bet, first, 75 min, a 150–300-line diff expected). The rest of the queue balances: b94 (kept from #91's plan — the punt to the eyot, the run's newest place that nobody can stand on; the second bet, medium); b96 a murmuration coming in to roost at dusk in autumn and winter — the roofline and the sky above the river are the top third of the wide shot and nothing flocks in it (Roofs & skyline × New element, the domain's first new thing); b97 the lane's morning — the morning lapse is one tap away and shows the sweeper and the cart and nobody else, and the lane has had no shipped work for twenty iterations; b93 (kept — three measured camera loose ends, low, last). Cost discipline for this batch: every count a brief needs is IN the brief; no brief opens with 'measure first'. If the next three rows come in over $10 with output flat, the next pass reads the turns column before it reads the town.

queue.brief: THE BET — rung 6, retire and rebuild the courtyard's population. The counts are DONE (probes/shade.mjs on HEAD, 10 seeds × summer days 5–7, warmth 0.97): the lawn's own kinds inside the wall hold a median 0.25 person at 10 h, 1.0 at 13 h, 2.0 at 16 h; at 13 h kid 0.43, napper 0.23, picnic 0.27, sitter 0, gardener 0; seed 42 at 13:25 on days 6 and 7 shows nobody. Do not re-measure — build. The cause is the iteration-1 model in the spawn loop (~line 7917): ONE `spawnAgent(room)` roll under `capacity = 2 + round(m·(3 + 9·daylight·yearBusy(EX_COURT)))` at `rate ≈ (0.05 + 0.42m)·(0.12 + daylight)`, where the default branch is a ring walker who crosses and leaves (~40 s = a resident) so `courtyardCount` is spent on transit, and the staying kinds are shares of that roll (gardener 0.10, kid 0.12, then dog/picnic/napper/sitter). The plaza (#92 spawnFamilyAgent/FAM_CAP), the cafe (#74), the warm evening (#79) each outgrew this; the courtyard is the last population still on it. Rebuild it their way: `spawnLawnAgent()` as the LAWN's own source, off `capacity`, with the lawn's PLACES as its cap — the 4 BENCH_SPOTS (sitters), shadeSpots()/napAt (nappers), the picnic annulus r 9–12 via picnicAt (pairs), the kid's run (kids, often two), EDGE_BEDS (one gardener) — each kind claiming a place at the choice and releasing it as the walk out begins; a visit priced at the choice against the retire rule (the sun ends a stay: `daylight`, SIT_REFUSE/seatRefused for the seated). Price presence as rate × visit BEFORE choosing the cap (law). Transit walkers/crossers/dogwalkers stay on the old roll under a `capacity` that no longer counts the stayers — then delete the staying branches from spawnAgent; a rebuild replaces, it does not bolt a second roll beside the first. Target: a summer 13 h holds 4–7 lawn-kind people on the MEDIAN seed (10 h ≥ 2, 16 h ≥ 3), every kind non-zero at 13 h across the sample, the lawn still empties by dark, rain and a clear winter noon stay within HEAD ± 1. A 150–300-line diff is expected and welcome; take the swing.

queue.brief: The punt to the eyot (c128). The island is the run's newest place and nobody can stand on it: the only way onto it is by water from the JETTY (128.4, 35; onJetty()), where overDeck()'s jetty visitors already stand for a while (a.stop at JETTY.x − 1.3). One count only, inline in the probe you write anyway (jetty stands/day and their dwell on HEAD, 10 seeds × 3 summer days — write the two numbers into the ledger and move on). Then: ONE punt moored at the jetty; in daylight, calm (windF < 0.5) and dry, a jetty visitor whose dwell allows it (priced at the CHOICE against their retire: the trip is ~1 h sim each way plus a stay) steps aboard, poles to the eyot's EAST shore (eyotShore; the channel and the rowboat's lane x 116.5–121.5 are never entered — the crossing runs x ≈ 127 → 126.2, rows 35 → 42, south of the deck rows 30..32), stands under the willow for 1–2 h sim (a.eyot; named 'someone on the eyot, under the willow'), poles back, and resumes their retrace. The punt is two draw items in the rowboat's idiom (drawBoat is the rowboat's: give the punt its own, hull + pole + figure), never under the deck; while it is out the mooring is empty. Swans already keep off the turf (offEyot) — make sure the punt's landing does not put a swan or a nesting duck ON the shore cell it lands at (the 0.9-cell law). __entities takes the punt and the a.eyot stander; one announce line as it pushes off.

queue.brief: A MURMURATION at dusk. The roofline and the sky over the river are the top third of every wide shot, and apart from chimney smoke and two vanes nothing moves up there; nothing in the town flocks. In autumn and winter (from the first shed day, leafShed() > 0.1, through midwinter to the first leafOut — read seasonPhase/leafShed/leafOut, do not invent a calendar), on a dry evening (not raining, windF < 0.7), a flock of starlings gathers over the river and far bank in the last stretch of daylight — time-compressed to ~1.2 h sim (~2.7 real s; a twenty-minute one would be 0.75 s and nobody would see it): forming from sunDown − 1.3 h, boiling and turning against the sky as one soft cloud (a particle FIELD of 80–160 dots with two or three drifting attractors and a per-particle hash phase — NOT birds[] agents), leaning downwind off windDir(), then funnelling down into a roost at sunDown − 0.1: the church tower and the far-bank ridges (CHURCH; the eyot's willow may take a share). At sunrise a thin skein leaves the roost. Draw it as ONE live pass between drawBackdrop and the roof rows so it passes BEHIND the spire and the clock tower, and let applyLight/nightF own its colour (it is dark against a bright sky, then gone). No R(): hash(day, k) for the day's flock size, hashes for phases — zero reshuffle, canvas IDENTICAL to HEAD with the season forced to summer. nameAt over the cloud: 'starlings coming in to roost'; one announce as it forms; the evening lapse (sunDown + 1) passes through it — the filmstrip of that lapse must show the cloud and must not POP when it dissolves into the roost (fade the roost's last particles over ≥ 0.3 s real).

The clock button's second landing (sunUp + 0.5, one tap away) shows the sweeper, the cart from ~sunUp + 0.2 and nobody else — the watch line says so and nobody has built for that hour. The lane has had no shipped work since #74. Give it a morning round: ONE figure with a handcart or a bag who comes in at the west end at sunUp − 0.3 and works the HOME_DOORS (y 64; x 4..130, fourteen doors) in order, a short stop at each (a bottle or a parcel left on the step: one small draw per delivered door, visible at 3×, cleared by ~09:30 as if taken in), out by the east end by sunUp + 1.6; its own source beside the sweeper's spawn (~line 3481: `!sweeper && hour > sunUp − 0.5 …`), NEVER a laneCap share; goes in rain under an umbrella (a.umbrella exists), skips only when snow is lying (snowCover > 0.5). Price the round first: fourteen stops must fit 1.9 h at effective speed ~0.75·a.speed — trace one; if it does not fit, fewer doors, not a faster walker. Second clause, the one a wide shot reads: the HOMES' windows are lit before sunrise — from sunUp − 0.8 fading out by sunUp + 0.4 — through windowLit()/LIT_PANES exactly as the evening does (check first whether a dawn is ALREADY lit by the nid mechanism; if it is, count it, say so, and spend the time on the round).
